## Purpose

This SOP establishes the procedures for managing the chemical inventory
in EA Program laboratories. A current, accurate inventory is essential
for safety (knowing what is on hand in an emergency), regulatory
compliance (fire code limits on flammable storage, Pomona College
Chemical Hygiene Plan), waste minimization (avoiding duplicate
purchases and expired stockpiles), and research efficiency (knowing
what is available before ordering) [@osha_labsafety2012; @nfpa45_2019].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All chemicals stored in EA Program laboratories
  (SGM 133, 134, 135), including reagents, standards, solvents, acids,
  bases, compressed gases, and prepared solutions
- **Does not apply to:** Common consumables that are not hazardous
  (Kimwipes, gloves, filter paper, etc.), or chemicals stored
  exclusively in other departments' spaces
- **Location:** All EA Program laboratory spaces


## Definitions

- **CAS number (Chemical Abstracts Service Registry Number):** A unique
  numerical identifier assigned to every chemical substance by CAS; the
  most reliable identifier for chemicals because, unlike common names,
  it is unambiguous; required on every inventory spreadsheet row.
- **Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP):** A written program required by OSHA's
  Laboratory Standard (29 CFR 1910.1450) describing the safety
  procedures, equipment, and work practices in place to protect
  laboratory workers from hazardous chemicals; Pomona College's CHP is
  maintained by EH&S [@osha_labsafety2012].
- **Expiration date:** The manufacturer-recommended date after which a
  chemical's stated purity, concentration, or safety characteristics
  may no longer be guaranteed; after this date, the chemical must be
  tested or disposed of.
- **GHS (Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of
  Chemicals):** The United Nations system for standardizing chemical
  hazard communication; governs the content and format of Safety Data
  Sheets and container labels in the United States under the OSHA
  Hazard Communication Standard [@osha_labsafety2012].
- **Hazard class:** A classification of a chemical's primary physical
  or health hazard (flammable, corrosive, oxidizer, toxic, carcinogen,
  etc.) per OSHA/GHS criteria; used to assign compatible storage
  locations and set fire code quantity limits [@nfpa45_2019].
- **NFPA 45:** The National Fire Protection Association standard
  governing fire protection for laboratories using chemicals; sets
  maximum allowable quantities (MAQs) of flammable and combustible
  liquids that may be stored in different lab occupancy types
  [@nfpa45_2019].
- **Peroxide-forming solvent:** A solvent that can spontaneously form
  explosive organic peroxides during storage (e.g., diethyl ether, THF,
  isopropanol); must be tested periodically with peroxide test strips
  and disposed of before the safe shelf life is exceeded; open-date
  label required on every container [@nrc_prudent2011].
- **Safety Data Sheet (SDS):** A standardized 16-section document (GHS
  format) describing a chemical's identity, hazards, safe handling,
  storage, disposal, and emergency response; legally required to be
  accessible in the workplace for all hazardous chemicals; Section 7
  (Handling and Storage) and Section 13 (Disposal) are most relevant
  to inventory management [@osha_labsafety2012].
- **Small Quantity Generator (SQG):** A US EPA RCRA designation for
  facilities generating 100--1,000 kg of hazardous waste per month;
  Pomona College's classification, which sets specific accumulation
  time and storage requirements.
- **Surrogate chemical:** A non-hazardous chemical used for training
  and demonstration purposes in place of a hazardous substance.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve purchases; ensure compliance with fire code limits |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain the inventory database; conduct audits         |
| All Lab Personnel | Log new chemicals upon receipt; update inventory when chemicals are consumed or disposed |
| Chemical Safety Officer | Review inventory for incompatibilities and compliance |


## Safety Considerations

Accurate inventory management is a safety measure [@osha_labsafety2012;
@nfpa45_2019]:

- First responders and the fire department use the chemical inventory
  to assess hazards during emergencies.
- NFPA 45 fire code limits the total quantity of flammable liquids that
  may be stored outside of approved flammable-storage cabinets
  [@nfpa45_2019].
- Knowing what is stored and where prevents accidental mixing of
  incompatible chemicals.
- Expired chemicals (especially peroxide-forming solvents) can become
  hazardous over time [@nrc_prudent2011].

See [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) for chemical
storage, compatibility, and labeling requirements.


## The Inventory System

### Electronic Inventory

The EA Program maintains a shared Google Sheet (or equivalent
spreadsheet) as the master chemical inventory. The spreadsheet is
stored on the lab shared drive and accessible to all lab personnel.

**Required columns:**

| Column              | Description                                      |
|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| Chemical name       | Full name (no abbreviations or formulas only)    |
| CAS number          | Chemical Abstracts Service registry number       |
| Manufacturer        | Supplier name                                    |
| Catalog number      | Supplier catalog/part number                     |
| Lot number          | Manufacturer lot number                          |
| Date received       | YYYY-MM-DD                                       |
| Quantity received   | Amount and units (e.g., 500 mL, 100 g)          |
| Current quantity    | Updated when significantly depleted              |
| Concentration/purity| If applicable (e.g., "ACS reagent grade, 37%")  |
| Expiration date     | From manufacturer label, or calculated shelf life|
| Hazard class        | Flammable, corrosive, oxidizer, toxic, etc.      |
| Storage location    | Room, cabinet/shelf code (e.g., SGM 133, Flam-1) |
| SDS on file         | Yes/No                                           |
| Owner/project       | Who ordered it and for what project               |
| Status              | In use / Sealed / Expired / Disposed             |

### Physical Labels

Every chemical container in the lab must have a label that includes:

- Chemical name (spelled out)
- Concentration (if a prepared solution)
- Hazard warning(s) per GHS
- Date received or date prepared
- Researcher name
- Expiration date (if applicable)

See [SOP-L003, Section 6.4](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
for detailed labeling requirements.


## Procedures

### Receiving New Chemicals

1. Inspect the container for damage, leaks, or missing labels when the
   shipment arrives.
2. If the container is damaged or leaking, do not accept it into the
   lab. Notify the lab manager. Follow spill procedures in
   [SOP-L004](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd) if needed.
3. Add the chemical to the inventory spreadsheet immediately,
   completing all required columns.
4. Verify that the SDS is on file. If not, download it from the
   manufacturer's website and add it to the SDS binder and the
   electronic SDS folder.
5. Label the container with the date received and the researcher's
   name if not already present.
6. Store the chemical in the correct location based on its hazard
   class (see §5.3).

### Ordering Chemicals

Before ordering a new chemical:

1. Check the inventory spreadsheet to see if the chemical is already
   in stock.
2. Check with other lab users to see if someone has an open container
   that can be shared.
3. Order only the quantity needed for the project. Purchasing excess
   chemicals generates waste and occupies storage space.
4. For highly hazardous chemicals, consult the PI and review the SDS
   before ordering [@nrc_prudent2011].

### Storage Assignment

Assign storage based on hazard class. Chemicals must be segregated by
compatibility [@nfpa45_2019]:

| Hazard Class       | Storage Location                              |
|:-------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| Flammable liquids  | Flammable-storage cabinet (yellow, self-closing) |
| Corrosive acids    | Acid cabinet (under fume hood) -- separate from bases |
| Corrosive bases    | Base cabinet (under fume hood) -- separate from acids |
| Oxidizers          | Separate from flammables and organics          |
| Toxics / reagents  | General chemical shelves, secured              |
| Compressed gases   | Chained to wall or bench; away from corrosives |
| Refrigerated/frozen| Lab refrigerator or freezer (no food)          |

::: {.callout-important}
Never store chemicals on the floor. Use low shelves or cabinets with
front lips. Ensure shelves are fastened to the wall. See
[SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd), Section 6.3
for detailed storage rules.
:::

### Using and Depleting Chemicals

- When you open a sealed container for the first time, write the date
  opened on the label.
- When a container is nearly empty or fully consumed, update the
  "Current quantity" and "Status" columns in the inventory spreadsheet.
- Return every chemical to its designated storage location after use.

### Disposing of Chemicals

When a chemical is expired, no longer needed, or in poor condition:

1. Update the inventory spreadsheet: change Status to "Disposed" and
   record the disposal date.
2. Follow the waste disposal procedures in
   [SOP-L003, Section 8](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd):
   fill out a waste tag, complete the packing manifest, and schedule
   pickup.
3. Do not pour chemicals down the drain unless explicitly permitted by
   the SDS and local regulations for that specific chemical.

### Periodic Audits

Conduct a full physical audit of the chemical inventory at least once
per year (typically at the start of the fall semester) [@nrc_prudent2011]:

1. Print the current inventory spreadsheet.
2. Walk through every storage location and physically verify each item.
3. Note discrepancies between the spreadsheet and actual stock.
4. Remove expired chemicals for disposal.
5. Update the spreadsheet to reflect the audit results.
6. File the annotated printout as the audit record.


## Waste Minimization

- Order the smallest quantity that will meet your needs.
- Share chemicals across projects when possible.
- Prepare only the volume of working solutions needed for an
  analytical session.
- Substitute less hazardous chemicals when feasible (e.g., replace a
  halogenated solvent with a non-halogenated alternative).
- Dispose of expired chemicals promptly rather than letting them
  accumulate.

See [SOP-L003, Section 8.3](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
for additional waste minimization guidance.

## Training Record

Before ordering, receiving, or storing chemicals independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate how to add a new chemical to the inventory spreadsheet
3. Locate SDS binders and the electronic SDS folder
4. Identify the correct storage location for a given hazard class
5. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
